title: Can “GTA V” Help Scientists Model Climate Change in L.A.? - Nautilus
author: Jake Currie
text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementEnvironmentCan “GTA V” Help Scientists Model Climate Change in L.A.?More importantly, can it get people to care?JCBy Jake Currie3:00 PM CST on November 18, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleYou can’t turn your head without seeing an advertisement for Grand Theft Auto VI. The ad blitz is reaching a crescendo because the highly anticipated eighth installment in the Rockstar Games franchise drops tomorrow, 13 years after the release of its predecessor, GTA V. And after such a long wait, the pressure to deliver is sky high.  Powered By 10 ShareNextStayAfter all, GTA V featured a meticulous and immersive recreation of Los Angeles (called Los Santos) based on field research, satellite maps, census data, and more. And Rockstar’s remarkable level of detail has stood the test of time, with many players returning to the game while they wait for the sequel. Climate scientists are apparently no different. In a new study published in Geoscience Communication, a team of researchers used the fictional city of Los Santos to model rising sea levels.  Read more: “Playing Video Games Makes Us Fully Human”Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
